title_zh: Harley Bassman（Convexity Maven）：这不是通胀问题，而是信任问题
subtitle_zh: MOVE 指数缔造者 Harley Bassman 剖析美国财政失控、长端利率与被动资金主导的市场。

turns.en: into the 95% fiscal problem. We got five trillion of income and seven trillion of expenses. Interest is now 1.1, 1.2 trillion. They're taking everything to the front end, right?
turns.zh: ……正是那 95% 的财政问题。我们收入 5 万亿，支出 7 万亿，利息支出现在到了 1.1 到 1.2 万亿。他们把所有东西都往短端推，对吧？

turns.en: They're issuing bills and buying back bonds. Kind of a clever idea that didn't work. If you were to go play this game long enough and we stay here and you mark 40 trillion at 5%, where once all the older debt, the low coupon debt rolls off, and the new debt comes out, we're talking two trillion dollars in just interest, which blows away defense spending and everything else.
turns.zh: 发国库券（T-bills）、回购长期债券。挺聪明的想法，但没起作用。如果这个游戏玩得够久，利率还停在这里，40 万亿债务按 5% 重新定价——等旧的、低票息的债务全部滚动到期、新债务发出来——光利息就高达 2 万亿美元，把国防开支和其他一切远远甩在身后。

turns.en: This is unsustainable. Hello, this is Dean Curnutt and welcome to the Alpha Exchange, where we explore topics in financial markets associated with managing risk, generating return, and the deployment of capital and the alternative investment industry.
turns.zh: 这是不可持续的。——大家好，我是 Dean Kernott，欢迎来到 Alpha Exchange。在这档节目里，我们探讨金融市场中与风险管理、收益创造以及另类投资行业资本配置相关的主题。

turns.en: I'm joined by the Maven of Convexity himself, Harley Bassman, at a time when rates are backing up and Harley's move index is north of 100. Harley, it's great to have you back on the podcast at a really interesting time for markets in the world.
turns.zh: 今天的嘉宾是凸性大师（Maven of Convexity）本人 Harley Bassman。此刻利率正在往上走，而 Harley 创造的 MOVE 指数已经超过 100。Harley，在市场和世界都处于一个非常有趣的时刻回到节目，太好了。

turns.en: Thank you, great to be back. I wish it was a tad more boring, to be told. So much going on. And I'll just start with an assertion that is kind of obvious, which is the causality of moves between the, let's say, rates market and the S&P is kind of reversed.
turns.zh: 谢谢，很高兴回来。我只希望事情能稍微无聊一点，要说的实在太多了。我先抛一个相当显而易见的论断：利率市场和标普之间的因果传导，已经被颠倒过来了。

turns.en: It's typically, the S&P's got some shock. It leads to a flight to safety and duration rallies. And you look at it these days, and it's the 10-year note, maybe the 30-year.
turns.zh: 通常是标普遭遇某种冲击，资金涌向避险，久期资产上涨。可你看看现在，领涨的却是 10 年期国债，也许是 30 年期。

turns.en: Those, to me, seem to be the risk assets driving the equity market. So those correlations are really positive. Right now, it seems pretty fragile.
turns.zh: 在我看来，它们才是驱动股市的风险资产。所以这些相关性变得非常正。而眼下的局面，看起来相当脆弱。

turns.en: I just love to start with your take. You're a 30 to 40-year veteran, I would say 40-year veteran, in rates and mortgages and analysis of risk.
turns.zh: 我想先从你的看法开始。你在利率、按揭和市场风险分析这个行当是 30 到 40 年的老兵——我会说是 40 年。

turns.en: Take us through your big picture of where we are here with, especially with the backup in long-end yields. I write a commentary, episodic, whatever I want to write.
turns.zh: 给我们讲讲你对当前局面、特别是长端收益率大幅上行的整体判断。——我写评论文章，断断续续，想写什么就写什么。

turns.en: They're posted on convexdomaven.com. I have my entire article here. Convexdomaven.com. I have my entire archive on there, going back, I don't know, over 20 years.
turns.zh: 都发在 convexdomaven.com 上，我所有的文章都在那里。convexdomaven.com，整个存档都在上面，往回追溯我不知道超过 20 年了。

turns.en: It's free, send me an email, I'll add you to my list. And my last commentary was entitled, In Fed We Trust. And what I'm proposing there is, we don't have an inflation problem, with rates going higher.
turns.zh: 免费，给我发封邮件，我把你加进邮件列表。我最新一篇评论的标题是《In Fed We Trust》。我在里面提出的观点是：随着利率走高，我们面对的不是通胀问题——

turns.en: We have a trust problem. We don't trust the government. We don't trust our institutions. Fed, we kind of trust maybe. But away from that, there's no control of our fiscal policy.
turns.zh: 而是信任问题。我们不信任政府，不信任我们的制度机构。美联储，也许还算有点信任。但除此之外，我们的财政政策完全失控。

turns.en: We're running a $2 trillion deficit, with a 4-2 unemployment rate, S&P near its high. We're not at war. Well, I guess maybe a skirmish right now, but it's unprecedented to have a 6% fiscal deficit, without being at war or being in a recession.
turns.zh: 我们在 4.2% 的失业率、标普接近历史高点的情况下，跑着 2 万亿美元的赤字。我们没有处于战争状态——好吧，也许算一些小冲突——但在既非战争也非衰退的时候维持 6% 的财政赤字，是史无前例的。

turns.en: And for the foreseeable future, is to keep on going. Are we gonna go bankrupt? No, we're not gonna go bankrupt. We issue dollars and we print dollars.
turns.zh: 而且在可预见的未来还会继续下去。我们会破产吗？不会，我们不会破产。我们发行美元，也印制美元。

turns.en: We can't go bankrupt. We can't default. Can we devalue that currency? Yeah. And I think what's happening here right now, is we're just seeing a lack of trust, locally and globally, in the US dollar.
turns.zh: 我们不可能破产，不可能违约。那我们能不能让货币贬值？能。我认为现在正在发生的，就是无论国内还是全球层面，对美元的信任在流失。

turns.en: Now, by the way, Western Europe is not much better. Japan clearly is not better. So I guess all paper or currency is getting devalued. And how do you know it's not inflation that's driving this thing?
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，西欧也没好到哪里去，日本显然更糟。所以我猜所有的纸币、所有的货币都在被稀释。——那你怎么知道推动这一切的不是通胀呢？

turns.en: If you look at the break-even tips. Now, I'm not a fan of tips. I'll tell you that. It's a small market, kind of controlled by a few people.
turns.zh: 去看盈亏平衡通胀率（breakeven TIPS）。我先把话撂这儿：我不喜欢 TIPS。这个市场很小，基本上被少数人控制。

turns.en: Nonetheless, it's been hovering at a 235 break-even rate for the last four years. We've had rates down and up, and it's been up and down at 235.
turns.zh: 但尽管如此，过去四年盈亏平衡率一直在 2.35% 附近徘徊。利率起起落落，它就待在 2.35% 上下。

turns.en: So the market is not pricing in a big inflation. And cores at two and change, it's not getting away from us. But rates are up 150 base points in the last X number of months.
turns.zh: 所以市场并没有定价大通胀。核心通胀在 2% 出头，没有失控。可过去一段时间利率上行了 150 个基点。

turns.en: This is a trust problem in the US. Why are stocks not breaking? It's not stock in the US government or in a dollar or currency. It's stocked in an entity that makes money and can raise prices with inflation.
turns.zh: 这是美国的信任问题。那股票为什么不崩？因为人们信心寄托的不是美国政府、不是美元或货币，而是能赚钱、能跟着通胀提价的企业。

turns.en: As a matter of fact, one of the best hedges against inflation is owning a stock that can raise their price and manage their business. If you bought stocks in Heimar, Germany, remember the guys with the real barrels?
turns.zh: 事实上，对抗通胀最好的对冲之一，就是拥有能提价、能经营好自己生意的股票。如果你在魏玛时期的德国买过股票——还记得那些真正靠卖桶发财的人吗？——

turns.en: If you bought those stocks and held them all the way through, you were fine because they just raised their prices along with everything else.
turns.zh: 如果你买了那些股票并一路持有，你没事，因为它们只是跟着所有东西一起涨价。

turns.en: And their businesses expanded. It sounds crazy, but that's what happened over there. And what we're seeing now, I like real estate, I suppose, but the idea of the US currency is suspect and we're pushing it back.
turns.zh: 它们的生意还在扩张。听起来疯狂，但那边确实就是这么发生的。而我们现在看到的是——我挺喜欢房地产——但美元这个概念本身开始可疑，我们正在把它往后推。

turns.en: In a nutshell, the big idea is, how do we get out of this problem? Well, you default or you inflate, or you can grow, I suppose, but I don't see growth as being a reasonable way to get out of this problem, this stage of the game.
turns.zh: 简单说，大问题就是：我们怎么从这个困局里走出去？要么违约，要么通胀，或者靠增长——但在现阶段，我不认为增长是走出这个困境的合理方式。

turns.en: And we're gonna inflate. Inflation is the only tax that both Republicans and Democrats can agree on because you never vote on it. It's a silent tax on the middle class.
turns.zh: 而我们会选择通胀。通胀是唯一一种共和党和民主党都能达成一致的税，因为你从来不用对它投票表决。它是对中产阶级的一道沉默的税。

turns.en: You can tax the billionaires to zero. It doesn't make a damn bit of a difference. You have to tax the middle class and inflation is that tax.
turns.zh: 你可以对亿万富翁征税征到零，那毫无意义。你必须向中产阶级征税，而通胀就是那道税。

turns.en: So that's kind of it. Let's drill down into the breakdown of nominal yields into their real and inflation components. And yeah, tips, you know a ton about this market.
turns.zh: 所以大致就是这样。——我们来深挖一下：把名义收益率分解成实际收益率和通胀预期两个部分。说到 TIPS，你对这个市场懂得非常多。

turns.en: I know a little bit about it. It's got its vagaries. It's got that illiquidity behavior, especially during significant risk offs. That embedded premium for inflation risk, I think two, three is roughly where tens are in terms of break events.
turns.zh: 我略懂一点。这个市场有自己的怪脾气，有那种流动性缺失的行为，尤其在重大避险时刻。里面内嵌的通胀风险溢价——我想大概在二点几、三左右——差不多就是 10 年期盈亏平衡的位置。

turns.en: That's pretty low. If you sort of look at nominal versus real in terms of taking risk and maybe lending to the government with some embedded some ways put on inflation or inflation protection, again, getting away from the vagaries of tips.
turns.zh: 那相当低。如果你从承担风险、把钱借给政府、内嵌某种对通胀的保护的角度看名义与实际收益率——再说一遍，抛开 TIPS 的怪脾气不谈——

turns.en: Does that two, three seem low to you in terms of inflation compensation? If you actually think about it, I've said 235 is the implied inflation rate, break even inflation rate.
turns.zh: 这个二点几，在你看来作为通胀补偿是不是偏低？

turns.en: Just take the 10 year nominal, 10 year tip, subtract the two, there you go. That's not quite right, but it's close enough for government work.
turns.zh: 你仔细想，我说过 2.35% 就是隐含通胀率、盈亏平衡通胀率。拿 10 年期名义减去 10 年期 TIPS 收益率，就是这么算。不完全准确，但够政府工程用了。

turns.en: It has a bunch in four years. What's wrong with this picture? What's wrong with this picture might be that CPI is cooked. Remember the government rejiggered CPI in the late 90s, re-inspanning Clinton and Reuben and everyone else.
turns.zh: 四年来它一直在晃。这画面里哪里不对劲？不对劲的地方可能是：CPI 被动过手脚。记得吗，政府在上世纪 90 年代末重新调整了 CPI，在 Clinton 和 Rubin 那一届。

turns.en: And they basically dialed it down with hedonics, asset replacement, like you stop buying beef and you buy chicken, quality improvement. And they did that for a reason.
turns.zh: 他们用享乐回归法（hedonics）、资产替代——比如你买不起牛肉就改买鸡肉——质量改进之类的办法把它调低了。他们这么做是有原因的。

turns.en: They want CPI to be low. They want it to be low because social security and other benefits are linked to CPI. So the extent they can keep CPI under the real growth in the system, then the government basically slows down their expenditures.
turns.zh: 他们希望 CPI 低。他们希望它低，因为社会保障和其他福利跟 CPI 挂钩。所以只要他们能把 CPI 压在体系的实际增长之下，政府实际上就放慢了自己的支出。

turns.en: Is that a public policy good? Yeah. I mean, especially right now, I'm in favor of that idea. But that could be why you see these tips real yield rising because people think that CPI understates real inflation.
turns.zh: 这算好的公共政策吗？算。我是说，尤其现在，我支持这个思路。但这也许正是你看到 TIPS 实际收益率上升的原因——因为大家认为 CPI 低估了真实的通胀。

turns.en: And this really kind of goes back to a bigger concept of what's going on here. Ma always said to not talk about politics or religion and play company.
turns.zh: 而这一切其实牵涉到一个更大的概念：这里到底在发生什么。我妈常说，别谈政治和宗教，好好做生意。

turns.en: So I'll kind of go with 30,000 feet. I would say that what you have going on with both Trump and Biden, Republicans and Democrats here, the individuals are not the problem.
turns.zh: 所以我就站在三万英尺的高度说。我要说的是，不管是 Trump 还是 Biden，共和党还是民主党，具体的人不是问题所在。

turns.en: It's a symptom. And the symptom is we have this, what's called a K economy, that's getting bigger and bigger. Simple example, what they're doing is they're using mean versus median.
turns.zh: 这是一种症状。症状就是我们这个所谓的 K 型经济（K economy）差距越来越大。简单的例子：他们在用平均数而不是中位数。

turns.en: They're using a mean, an average. If you look at the average of the GDP and per capita and everything else, things look great. What's really happening is you have a village of 10 people.
turns.zh: 他们用的是均值、平均数。如果你看 GDP 的平均值、人均数字和其他一切，一切都显得很好。真实情况是，你有一个 10 个人的村子。

turns.en: Nine people are making 10,000 a year. One guy is making 500,000 a year. So your median person is making 10,000. Your average person is making 50 and change.
turns.zh: 九个人年收入 1 万美元，一个人年收入 50 万美元。所以中位数收入是 1 万美元，而平均数是 5 万出头。

turns.en: And they're quoting 50 and change in the press and the government, but no one's making 50. Almost everyone's making 10 for one guy making 500.
turns.zh: 媒体和政府报的都是 5 万出头，可没有人在赚 5 万。几乎所有人都赚 1 万，外加一个人赚 50 万。

turns.en: And that's the problem here is that the economy has been kept aloft by the spending and the income of the 1%, 0.1%, 5%, 10%, whatever I call at the top end.
turns.zh: 这就是问题所在：整个经济是靠 1%、0.1%、5%、10%——随你怎么叫——顶端那群人的收入和支出撑起来的。

turns.en: They're making money and spending everything else and everywhere else down below is getting killed. Why are they getting killed? Because if you look at the core costs of the big stuff, let's look at like an MBA starting salary from 35, 40 years ago, that number is basically doubled from 30, 40 years ago.
turns.zh: 他们在赚钱、在消费，而下面的其他地方全被挤压。为什么被挤压？因为如果你看看核心大项成本——比如 35、40 年前 MBA 的起薪——

turns.en: Housing up four to five X, healthcare up four to five X, college up four to five X. That's the disconnect here is that my kids, my millennials, they really can't afford to live anywhere, live in the city at least, because the real big numbers are up four to five X while incomes up is doubled.
turns.zh: 那个数字基本上只翻了一倍，而房价涨了 4 到 5 倍，医疗涨了 4 到 5 倍，大学学费涨了 4 到 5 倍。这就是脱节所在：我的孩子们，千禧一代，真的负担不起在任何地方生活，至少在城市里——因为真正的大头涨了 4 到 5 倍，收入只翻了一倍。

turns.en: And this is showing up everywhere in the system. While you see confidence going down, right wrong direction going down is the bulk of the deal.
turns.zh: 而这种现象在体系里到处都是。你会看到信心在下滑——方向不对，而这正是问题的主体。

turns.en: So it's a mean median average situation and the politicians are sticking to the mean that the reality is median is what's important over here.
turns.zh: 所以这就是均值和中位数的区别：政客们盯着均值，而现实是，中位数才是这边真正重要的。

turns.en: And those costs are going up much faster than inflation, CPI inflation, real inflation is going up much bigger. So that's what's kind of happening here.
turns.zh: 这些成本涨得比 CPI 通胀快得多，真实的通胀要高得多。所以大致就是这里正在发生的事。

turns.en: There's a lot of debate around the backup in 10s and 30s and yield and attribution. It's a very popular sport on Wall Street trying to determine the why of it.
turns.zh: 围绕 10 年期和 30 年期收益率上行的归因有很多争论。在华尔街，弄清为什么是一项非常热门的运动。

turns.en: And people get very defensive about their own view. Some suggest it's just a string of forwards, 10s are up, cause twos are up. And I think a bit more in your camp, which is there's something else going on here.
turns.zh: 人们对自己的观点往往很防御。有人说是纯粹的一系列远期传导：10 年期涨是因为 2 年期涨。而我更偏向你们那一派：这里还有别的东西在起作用。

turns.en: There is maybe a confidence premium. You and I share some University of Chicago lineage, Milton Friedman, inflation is everywhere and always a monetary phenomenon.
turns.zh: 也许存在一种信心溢价。你和我都有一点芝加哥大学的渊源——Milton Friedman——通胀永远、在所有地方都是一个货币现象。

turns.en: Maybe we throw fiscal in there as well, just back to the why of the more recent sell-off in the long end. It comes with higher short end yields as well.
turns.zh: 也许我们还该把财政也放进去。回到长端这波抛售的为什么，它是伴随着短端收益率一起上行的。你会怎么从构成要素上把这件事拆解开来？

turns.en: How would you just stylistically try to break it down in terms of the components? It is a 95% fiscal problem. We got five trillion of income and seven trillion of expenses.
turns.zh: 这是 95% 的财政问题。我们收入 5 万亿，支出 7 万亿，利息现在 1.1 到 1.2 万亿。

turns.en: Interest is now 1.1, 1.2 trillion. They're taking everything to the front end. They're issuing bills and buying back bonds. Kind of a clever idea that didn't work.
turns.zh: 他们把所有东西都推到短端——发国库券、回购债券。挺聪明的想法，但没管用。

turns.en: If you were to go play this game long enough and we stay here and you mark 40 trillion at 5%, once all the older debt, the low coupon debt rolls off, the new debt comes out, we're talking two trillion dollars in just interest, which blows away defense spending and everything else.
turns.zh: 如果这个游戏玩得足够久，利率还停在这儿，40 万亿债务按 5% 重估——等旧的、低息票的债务滚出去、新债务发出来——光利息就是 2 万亿美元，把国防开支和其他一切甩开几条街。

turns.en: This is unsustainable. It's unsustainable and I do not know how it's gonna end. I have ideas of what we could do today. We don't have to actually solve the problem today.
turns.zh: 这是不可持续的。不可持续，而且我不知道它会怎么收场。我有今天就可以做的一些想法。我们不必真的今天就解决问题。

turns.en: Even in 10 years, all we need is a path that's agreed upon that we're gonna go and start to do something. Right now, there's no path. There's no control.
turns.zh: 哪怕 10 年后，我们只需要一条大家认可的路线，表明我们要开始做点什么。而现在，没有路线，没有约束。

turns.en: There's no nothing. To the extent we recreate, like Clinton did with Social Security, Simpson-Bowles, any of these ideas that start to create a path for control, that'll solve the problem.
turns.zh: 什么都没有。如果我们能重新做出类似 Clinton 处理社会保障那样的改革、Simpson-Bowles 委员会，任何能建立起一条控制之路的想法，那就能解决问题。

turns.en: Right now, we have no problem. It's a trust problem. And both Democrats and Republicans, are they acting rationally? That's the problem. They kind of are, because they're in office for two, five, 10 years, and they're gone.
turns.zh: 现在我们不是没有意识到问题——这是个信任问题。民主党和共和党的所作所为理性吗？这就是问题所在。从某种意义上他们是理性的，因为他们当政 2 年、5 年、10 年，然后就走了。

turns.en: And they wanna get reelected. That's their goal is to get reelected. And so why should they sacrifice their careers, which they kind of like, it's kind of fun being a senator, why should they sacrifice their career for the benefit of someone in the future?
turns.zh: 他们想要连任，连任就是他们的目标。那他们为什么要牺牲自己的职业生涯——他们其实挺享受的，当参议员挺有意思——为什么要为了未来某个人的利益牺牲事业？

turns.en: That used to be called society. Now it's called something else, which is gonna have a deeper problem. That's it, man. We need to go. I got a path to bringing things under control.
turns.zh: 那过去叫社会。现在叫别的名字了，而这会带来更深层的问题。就是这么回事，伙计。我们需要一条把一切重新管住的路径。

turns.en: And if we do that, you'll see risk come down. A very prominent University of Chicago professor, Gene Fama has done tons of work over time on agency costs.
turns.zh: 如果我们这么做，你会看到风险降下来。——一位非常著名的芝加哥大学教授 Gene Fama，多年来做了大量关于代理成本（agency costs）的研究。

turns.en: And as you talk about the difficulty of solving this, and as you said, the short-term gain from a political standpoint, versus the longer-term potential payoff, this is a real agency problem, to try to dig in on this sort of thing.
turns.zh: 当你谈到解决这件事的难度——正如你说的，政治上的短期收益对比长期的潜在回报——这确实是一个经典的代理问题，值得深挖。

turns.en: What's your sense around, Scott Besen talking about buybacks, and drawing a little bit of a line in the sand. He hasn't said much recently as rates have risen.
turns.zh: 你怎么看 Scott Bessent 谈论回购、画下那道界线？随着利率上行，他最近话说得不多了。

turns.en: Is there some point at which Besen's got to come back? Is the path higher in rates just one way? How do you kind of see this thing playing out in the next month or so?
turns.zh: 会不会有某个时点 Bessent 不得不退回来？利率上行是一条单行道吗？接下来一个月左右，你怎么看这件事的演变？

turns.en: Buying that two, three, four trillion of long bonds, really? Like we have a $40 trillion deficit, man. I'm not gonna use the expression about what you're doing in the ocean, but that's what it is.
turns.zh: 买入那 2 万亿、3 万亿、4 万亿的长期债券？真的吗？我们有 40 万亿的债务，伙计。我不会用那句往海里做什么的粗话，但那就是实质。

turns.en: He's doing it for only a limited amount of time. It actually makes things worse. He looks weak because there's no plan. When Trump had Pultigo and had Fannie ready by $200 billion in mortgage bonds, that's not gonna dent anything.
turns.zh: 他这么做只能撑一小段时间，实际上让情况更糟。他显得软弱，因为没有计划。当年 Trump 想安排买入 2000 亿美元的 Fannie 按揭支持证券——那不会在任何东西上留下痕迹。

turns.en: Talking to a seven trillion dollar market. We tightened by a dime for a week or two, and then gave it right back. These aren't plans. They're like, I don't know, short-term coin flips.
turns.zh: 在一个 7 万亿美元的市场里。我们收紧了一角钱，持续了一两个星期，然后又原样还了回去。这些不是计划。它们像——我不知道——短期的抛硬币。

turns.en: We need to have a legit plan to do it. It may involve the Fed Treasury Agreement, not like 1951, but something like that. It's gonna involve the Fed pulling rates down at some point in the front end.
turns.zh: 我们需要一个真正像样的计划。它可能涉及一份美联储-财政部协议，不一定像 1951 年那份，但类似的东西。它将涉及美联储在某一点上把短端利率拉下来。

turns.en: The thing is, I see what, Warsh is trying to go and gain credibility. So my last two commentaries have both said, which was from in July, hike by 50.
turns.zh: 事情是这样的：我看 Warsh 是在试图赢得信誉。所以我最近两篇评论——最早那篇是 7 月写的——都说：加息 50。

turns.en: Hike 50, one and done, show that you're not beholden to Trump. Most other people are, that you're independent, and then you're gonna go look at the data.
turns.zh: 加息 50，一次搞定，表明你不被 Trump 牵制——大多数其他人都被他牵制——表明你是独立的，然后再去看数据。

turns.en: I don't like dots. I don't like forward guidance. All those things do is create moral hazard. Like I would describe the 060708 market blow-up.
turns.zh: 我不喜欢点阵图，我不喜欢前瞻指引。这些东西制造的全是道德风险（moral hazard）。就像我会用它来形容 06-07-08 那场市场崩盘。

turns.en: So Greenspan's measured pace. Remember, what he started doing in 2004, he said, we're gonna raise rates at a measured pace. And a measured pace meant 25 basis points every six weeks.
turns.zh: 想想 Greenspan 的渐进。记得吗，他 2004 年开始做的事：他说我们将以渐进的节奏加息。渐进节奏的意思是每六周加 25 个基点。

turns.en: Well, every hedge fund in the world basically said, well, I'm gonna go sell a six-week, 27 basis point out of the money put, because he knew it was 25.
turns.zh: 于是全世界几乎每个对冲基金都说：好，那我就卖出六周后到期、27 个基点价外的看跌期权，因为我知道一定是 25。

turns.en: And everyone got over their skis, levered long because he'd given us forward guidance that they weren't gonna go into any surprises and everyone just took massive risk.
turns.zh: 所有人都滑雪滑过了头，加杠杆做多——因为他给了前瞻指引说不会有意外，于是大家全都押上了巨大的风险。

turns.en: Why in Silicon Valley bank blow-up? Easy, because in 21-22, the Fed said, we are gonna keep rates at zero until early 2023. Go look it up. It's right in the comments he sent from the podium there.
turns.zh: 硅谷银行（Silicon Valley Bank）为什么爆雷？很简单，因为 2021-22 年美联储说过：我们将把利率维持在零附近直到 2023 年初。你们可以去查，就在他站在讲台上发表的讲话里。

turns.en: So obviously, you just go buy long-duration securities, don't hedge them until late 2022. That's what you do. Oh, I hedge them, but that's totally what they're gonna do.
turns.zh: 那么显然，你就去买长久期证券，一直不做对冲，直到 2022 年末——这就是你会做的。哦，我会对冲？不，这就是所有人当时认定他们会做的事。

turns.en: Moral hazard, kaboom, it changed policy. It's better that we don't even give a hint of what they're gonna be doing and let risk management run the business.
turns.zh: 道德风险，轰——它改变了政策。最好他们连一点暗示都不要给，让风险管理来经营生意。

turns.en: Because right now you have people looking at what the Fed's saying and then betting on that. Less you know, the less risk you're gonna take.
turns.zh: 因为现在的人是盯着美联储说了什么，然后押注那个。你越少知道，你冒的风险就越小。

turns.en: So I do think that we're kind of searching for that level right now and to go from there. But at some point, what I worry about is a death spiral.
turns.zh: 所以我确实认为我们当下正在寻找那个水平，然后从那里出发。但在某一点上，我担心的是一场死亡螺旋。

turns.en: I mean, if we keep running two trillion a year and there's no controls on this thing, we keep taking up the debt, keep taking up the interest payments.
turns.zh: 我是说，如果我们继续每年 2 万亿的赤字，对这一切没有任何约束，债务越堆越高，利息越付越多——

turns.en: At some point, it can't end well. That by the way, it could take 20 years for this to happen. Don't go short on the market yet. I do think that we need to gain credibility.
turns.zh: 到某个程度，它不可能有好结局。顺便说一句，这一切也许要花 20 年才会发生。现在还别做空市场。我确实认为我们需要重建信誉。

turns.en: I never believed in the word transitory three, four, five years ago. I kind of believe in it now because oil is a transitory cost. I mean, it will come down.
turns.zh: 三、四、五年前我从没相信过暂时性（transitory）这个词。现在我倒有点信了，因为石油是一个暂时性的成本——我是说，它会降下来。

turns.en: The war will end. I'm not sure when, but it will come down. And oil is not sensitive to the fed's rate. So therefore, there's really no correlation to that.
turns.zh: 战争会结束。我不确定什么时候，但它会结束，油价也会下来。而石油对美联储的利率并不敏感，所以两者之间其实没有相关性。

turns.en: Also, I'm not a believer that rates actually have that much of an impact anyways. Front-end rates have that thing of an impact. You've seen non-bank, private credit guys explode into the market, almost stepping into the shoes of the banks.
turns.zh: 另外，我从来不信利率本身有那么大的影响。短端利率确实有影响。你已经看到非银的私募信贷（private credit）玩家爆发式进入市场，几乎接过了银行的班。

turns.en: The banks basically are driven by the fed. They bar from the fed. They report to the fed. They have rules and regulations. So you take front-end rates up and the banks will raise their cost to see per se in I-Loans.
turns.zh: 银行基本上是被美联储驱动的。它们向美联储借款，向美联储汇报，受规则和监管约束。所以你把短端利率抬上去，银行就会提高自身的资金成本，进而提高贷款利率。

turns.en: Private credit doesn't care about that. Only care a little bit. But I mean, they really are not beholden to the fed. So the fed doesn't control that spigot.
turns.zh: 私募信贷不在乎这个，只在乎一点点。但我是说，他们真的不受美联储节制。所以美联储控制不了那个水龙头。

turns.en: And the hyperscalers, so we're gonna borrow new money, new debt, two trillion this year, more or less. I mean, we're gonna issue like four trillion of debt as we kind of roll over the stuff, but two trillion of new debt.
turns.zh: 然后是超大规模云服务商（hyperscalers）：今年我们要借新钱、新债，差不多 2 万亿。我是说，加上滚动到期，我们会发大约 4 万亿的债，但其中 2 万亿是新增。

turns.en: Hyperscaler estimates, the five big companies is 750 billion. We're talking like a third of what the government's borrowing on top of what the government's doing.
turns.zh: 对五家大型 hyperscalers 的估计是 7500 亿。相当于在政府自己的借款之上，又多了大约三分之一的量。

turns.en: And they are totally rate insensitive. They can borrow at six, eight, 10, 12. It just doesn't matter because these five guys know only one or two of them are gonna live.
turns.zh: 而它们对利率完全不敏感。它们能在 6%、8%、10%、12% 借款，无所谓，因为这五家心里清楚，最后只能活下一两家。

turns.en: And so it doesn't matter the price is they've got to go do it or they're gonna have a problem. So that's their fight. And therefore they will issue any price.
turns.zh: 所以价格无所谓——它们必须去做，不做就有麻烦。这是它们的生死之战。因此无论什么价格它们都会发债。

turns.en: It just doesn't matter. And by the way, they're probably money good. There's all five of them all in poor businesses that produce cash. So they can cover their coupon payments.
turns.zh: 就是无所谓。顺便说一句，它们大概是 money good 的。这五家做的都是能产生现金的生意，所以它们付得起票息。

turns.en: And I'm pretty sure they could probably cover their principal payments down the road. The equity guy, now he might take a hit, but the bond guy, you're probably money good on those things.
turns.zh: 而且我相当确定，将来它们也付得起本金。持股的股东嘛，可能会挨一刀；但持债的人，这些东西大概率是保本的。

turns.en: But nonetheless, any entity that buys a hyperscaler bond is not buying a treasury bond. So that pushes the entire complex up in rate. So that's why you're seeing this continued pressure in the 10-year sector and the 30-year sector.
turns.zh: 但话虽如此，任何一个买 hyperscaler 债券的主体，买的就不是美国国债。所以整个利率中枢都被往上推。这就是为什么 10 年期板块和 30 年期板块持续承压。

turns.en: And also in the very back end, who buys a 30-year bond? Nobody. I mean, insurance and pensions. Insurance and pensions are after a couple of decades of being underfunded, but they're now solvent basically.
turns.zh: 还有最长期端，谁会买 30 年期债券？没几个人。我是说，保险和养老金。在被掏空了几十年之后，保险和养老金现在基本上恢复了偿付能力。

turns.en: They can go and buy 30-year treasuries, 30-year corporates, whatever else, and be totally devised all the way out. They might even have a surplus now because of the stock market and where they're discounting their liabilities at.
turns.zh: 它们可以去买 30 年期国债、30 年期公司债之类的，把久期缺口完全覆盖掉。它们现在甚至可能有盈余，因为股市表现和它们折现负债所用的利率。

turns.en: They're running out of gas and of course Japan, Japan is gonna buy fewer treasuries. They're not gonna hit the bin cell, but they're gonna buy fewer because the spread between USD and JPY rates, after you include the hedging cost, has compressed significantly.
turns.zh: 它们的弹药快用完了。当然还有日本，日本会买更少的国债。他们不会清仓甩卖，但会少买，因为美元和日元的利差，计入对冲成本之后，已经大幅收窄。

turns.en: When Japan rates were zero or a quarter or a half and US rates were three or four, it made sense for the Japanese life companies or Manpah, Watanabe to go and buy structured products that took advantage of the rate spread.
turns.zh: 当日本利率是零、0.25 或 0.5，而美国利率是 3、4 的时候，日本寿险公司或者渡边太太（Watanabe）式的投资者，去买利用利差的结构化产品是说得通的。

turns.en: That doesn't exist anymore. And the currency's gotten annihilated. That too kind of helped. I just see less buying out of foreigners for US dollars.
turns.zh: 那个机会不复存在了。而且日元汇率也被摧毁了，这也推了一把。我就是觉得外国人买美元资产的量会更少。

turns.en: They're probably gonna buy gold. Gold's going down right now. Why is that? Well, one rate you're going up, and number two is you probably have people selling gold because when you get a margin called, man, you sell what you can, not what you want to.
turns.zh: 他们多半会去买黄金。可黄金现在在跌，为什么？第一，利率在升；第二，多半有人在被迫卖黄金——当被追保证金时，伙计，你卖的是你能卖的，不是你想卖的。

turns.en: And gold is still, you know, at 4,000 is well above where it was two years ago. I just think you're having a flight out of Western paper into other stuff, including stocks.
turns.zh: 而黄金现在在 4000，仍然远高于两年前的位置。我只是觉得，这是一场从西方纸币逃向其他资产的迁移，包括股票。

turns.en: So step back and maybe just try to give us the big picture of like the ecosystem of supply and demand for quote unquote safe assets. Let's say the Treasury complex.
turns.zh: 那么退一步，试着给我们描绘一下所谓安全资产——比如说国债这个体系——供求生态的全貌。

turns.en: And you've hit on a bunch of this. You've got, let's say Japan as a vehicle that put a lot of its excess savings in treasuries. Of course, China's way down from its peak in terms of US Treasury holdings.
turns.zh: 你已经讲到了其中很多。比如说，日本作为一个主体，把大量国民超额储蓄放进了国债。当然，中国持有美债的规模也已远低于其峰值。

turns.en: The Fed is no longer a source of significant demand as it was. How would you describe the change in the buyer base and how that's maybe interacting with the clearing price?
turns.zh: 美联储不再是重要的需求来源。你怎么描述买方结构的变化，以及它如何影响成交清算价？

turns.en: Do you think that alone is leading to just a softening in the back end and higher yields? To what extent? I think it's just supply. It's a fiscal situation out of control with the hyperscalers.
turns.zh: 你觉得单是这一点，就在导致长端走软、收益率走高吗？——在多大程度上？我觉得纯粹就是供给：财政失控，再加上 hyperscalers。

turns.en: It's just a supply issue. The buyers haven't changed all that much. And the foreigners a little bit, I suppose, but I mean, I just think it's a supply issue.
turns.zh: 就是供给问题。买家结构没有太大变化，外国人可能有一点变化，我猜。但我真的认为这是个供给问题。

turns.en: Well, let me circle back to something you were asking about on the real rate of tips and is 253% looking at 5s, 10s, 30s. Is that rich or cheap?
turns.zh: 那我们回到你之前提到的 TIPS 实际利率——看 5 年、10 年、30 年期，大概是 2.53%——这是贵还是便宜？

turns.en: My answer is I think it's crazy cheap. Assuming that CPI is a legit measure of inflation, it's your own experience, which maybe it's not. But to the extent you can get a real rate of 2 and 1 half, I think that's a pretty fancy rate.
turns.zh: 我的回答是：我觉得便宜得离谱。前提是 CPI 是一个正当的通胀度量——按你自己的经验，也许它不是。但如果你能拿到 2 个半百分点的实际利率，我觉得这是相当漂亮的收益率。

turns.en: When you think of that, if I got $2,000, I could put it in the cookie jar. I got $10,000, $20,000, $50,000 to put it under the mattress. You got a billion dollars?
turns.zh: 你想想看：如果我有 2000 美元，可以放进饼干罐。有 1 万、2 万、5 万美元，可以塞在床垫底下。可如果你有 10 亿美元呢？

turns.en: You can't put it in the mattress, man. You got to go and put it somewhere. The reason why you saw T-bills go negative yield in the US in 08, forget the Fed nonsense, and you saw a negative yield in the Depression, well, it's where else can you put your money?
turns.zh: 你没法把它塞床垫底下，伙计。你总得找个地方放。2008 年美国国库券收益率为什么会变成负的——别扯美联储那些话——以及大萧条时为什么也是负的：因为你的钱还能放在哪儿？

turns.en: It's safe that someone's not going to go and steal it or it's going to get caught in a house fire or who knows what might happen to it. You can't put large sums of money in cash somewhere to store it.
turns.zh: 放在那里安全：没人会来偷，不会有房子着火，谁知道还会发生什么。那么大一笔现金，你没法随便找个地方存起来。

turns.en: And so the extent that you can get any kind of return on basically cash, it's a good deed. So if you can get a real rate of half to 1%, that sounds totally fine to me from a safety standpoint.
turns.zh: 所以，只要你能在这种基本上等同于现金的东西上得到任何回报，那就功德一件。如果你能拿到 0.5% 到 1% 的实际利率，从安全性角度我觉得完全没问题。

turns.en: I think these real rates are crazy cheap to the extent CPI reflects reality, and that's the rub. But I mean, you're taking no risk with these things once you back up the inflation because there cannot be a default.
turns.zh: 我认为这些实际利率便宜得离谱——只要 CPI 反映现实，而这正是症结所在。但我是说，当你把通胀补回来之后，持有这些东西根本不承担风险，因为不可能违约。

turns.en: That can't happen. And by the way, if you think Fannie and Freddie are going to default, then my advice is gold guns in Kansatuna. That's where we're going to be if they default.
turns.zh: 那不可能发生。顺便说一句，如果你觉得 Fannie 和 Freddie 会违约，那我的建议是：黄金、枪支、金枪鱼罐头。它们要是违约，我们就到那步田地了。

turns.en: The flip side of the real rate from the lender standpoint, so the lender enjoying a high real rate, is the borrower paying a high real rate, and that could be viewed as restrictive.
turns.zh: 从出借人角度看实际利率的另一面——出借人享受高实际利率的另一面，是借款人在支付高实际利率——这可以被视作紧缩性的。

turns.en: We've talked a little bit in some ways about financial conditions. Warsh has brought that up at his most recent press conference. He says, it really depends on where you look.
turns.zh: 我们从某种程度上聊过金融条件（financial conditions）。Warsh 在最近一次记者会上也提到，他说这真的取决于你看哪里。

turns.en: And I think you're hitting on, it's probably still very cheap capital to meta by an optionality effectively with that debt pursuing AI riches, probably not so much for the mortgage potential person taking out a mortgage.
turns.zh: 我觉得你点到了：对 Meta 这样有效利用那份债务换取期权、追逐 AI 财富的公司来说，资本大概仍然非常便宜；而对一个正准备申请按揭的普通购房者，恐怕就不是了。

turns.en: I think we're at 7.2 now for the average 30 year. Take us through mortgage market dynamics. How restrictive do you think that is? And bigger picture, what's the Fed trying to accomplish right now and where are they relative to where you think they need to go in terms of making financial conditions restrictive enough to slow inflation?
turns.zh: 我想 30 年期平均按揭利率现在是 7.2%。带我们过一遍按揭市场的动态。你觉得这有多紧缩？更大的图景是：美联储现在想达成什么？在把金融条件紧缩到足以压住通胀这件事上，他们距离你认为他们需要到达的位置还有多远？

turns.en: The Fed's in a box. I mean, I don't know what the hell they're going to go and do. If they raise rates, they're going to go and make homeownership worse, which is a bad public policy, and they're going to go and basically cost you government more.
turns.zh: 美联储被困住了。我是说，我不知道他们到底会干什么。如果他们加息，会让购房变得更糟，这是很糟糕的公共政策，而且基本上让政府花更多钱。

turns.en: They take rates down. They're going to inflame inflationary fears and the back end's going to be totally out of control. The government just basically screwed this up for short-term reasons.
turns.zh: 他们降息，就会点燃通胀恐慌，长端会完全失控。政府就是出于短期考虑把这件事彻底搞砸了。

turns.en: I mean, QE was never a good idea. QE1 was a good idea. We are a financial economy. In fact, the West is basically a financial economy, which is a good thing.
turns.zh: 我是说，QE 从来不是好主意。QE1 是好主意。我们是一个金融经济体。事实上整个西方基本上都是一个金融经济体，这是好事。

turns.en: We're just pure with the gold standard. You're very restrictive of how much you can grow the economy because you couldn't grow money supply because it was dependent on how much gold you could mine.
turns.zh: 在金本位下，你能把经济增长到什么程度受到极严格的限制，因为你无法扩张货币供给——那取决于你能挖出多少金子。

turns.en: Going off the gold standard was not a bad thing, per se. And floating rates also is a good thing as it allocates capital to the right place.
turns.zh: 脱离金本位本身不是坏事。浮动利率也是好事，因为它把资本配置到该去的地方。

turns.en: Those are both good things. But the problem is, as a financial economy, you need plumbing. You got to go and get the money from the borrower to the lender.
turns.zh: 这两件都是好事。但问题是，作为一个金融经济体，你需要管道。你得把钱从借款人手上送到贷款人手上。

turns.en: Wall Street sits in between. And we have these pipes that move money around. 1809, there was a threat that the plumbing would get destroyed.
turns.zh: 华尔街坐在中间。我们有这些管道把钱来回搬运。2008-09 年，一度有威胁说这些管道会被摧毁。

turns.en: That happens. We're all doomed. So saving the banking system, then, yeah, there should have been guys that went to jail. There's no question.
turns.zh: 那会发生什么呢？我们都完了。所以当年拯救银行体系——是的，本来应该有人坐牢的。毫无疑问。

turns.en: We had people in jail after the 88 to 91 SNL crisis. I had seen no reason why we couldn't put people in jail for the 07 to 09 debacle. My ex-boss at Maryland should have been in jail.
turns.zh: 88 到 91 年的储贷（S&L）危机之后，我们确实把人送进了监狱。我想不出为什么 07 到 09 年那场灾难我们不能把人送进监狱。我在 Maryland 的前老板本该坐牢。

turns.en: But there are a lot of bad guys there, and the government didn't prosecute them and they should have. Or at least even if we're going to win in court, just tie them up in litigation for a couple of years to go and signal to people that there's a cost to doing evil deeds, even if it's not illegal.
turns.zh: 那里确实有很多坏人，而政府没有起诉他们，本该起诉。或者哪怕打不赢官司，就把他们拖在诉讼里两三年，向人们传递一个信号：作恶是有代价的，即使那些事不违法。

turns.en: But now we're in a situation where I'm not sure how we get out of this thing easily without debasing the currency. That's going to be what we have, but we're going to debase the currency.
turns.zh: 但现在我们身处这样的局面：我不确定除了让货币贬值，我们能有什么容易的出路。贬值的货币将会是我们的结局。

turns.en: I'm not sure versus what. I mean, Japan, look, everyone says in Japan, how are they possibly going to go and have a 200% or 300% debt to GDP ratio?
turns.zh: 只是我不确定是相对于什么贬值。我是说，日本——大家一直在问：日本怎么可能扛住 200% 甚至 300% 的债务/GDP 比率？

turns.en: How is this possible? We're currently going from 80 to 160. That's what's possible, right? That's the escape valve. The US dollar will go down the same path, I suppose, at some point.
turns.zh: 这怎么可能？我们目前正从 80% 走向 160%。这就是正在发生的事，对吧？那是泄压阀。我猜美元在某个时点也会走同一条路。

turns.en: I'm not sure versus what. But that's kind of it. Owning paper money is tough right now. Housing, it's unaffordable, basically, for most people.
turns.zh: 我不确定是相对于什么。但大致就是这样。现在持有纸币很难。住房，对绝大多数人来说基本上负担不起。

turns.en: Once again, going back to the K-shaped economy, media versus meme, this is a symptom of what's going on, but your median person can't buy your median house.
turns.zh: 再说一遍，回到 K 型经济，中位数对比平均数——这是正在发生的事情的一个症状：中位数收入的人买不起中位数价格的房子。

turns.en: Your rich millennials are boomers. I guess they could buy or help make down payments for their millennial kids, the rich ones can, which is what's been happening.
turns.zh: 富裕的千禧一代其实是婴儿潮一代。我猜他们自己买，或者帮他们的千禧代孩子出首付——有钱的可以，这也正是一直在发生的。

turns.en: But your average median person can't buy your median home. You see this in the affordability index. It went well below 100 and incomes are rising that fast and house prices have not come down by that much.
turns.zh: 但普通的、中位数收入的人买不了中位数的房子。这能从房价负担能力指数看出来：它远低于 100，收入有涨那么快吗？房价也没下来多少。

turns.en: You take rates up, you reduce the number of people that can afford to buy a median house. This is not good and housing is 18% of the economy.
turns.zh: 你把利率抬高，能买得起中位数住房的人数就减少。这不是好事，而住房占经济的 18%。

turns.en: I suppose the back end going up will eventually throw us into a recession, which theoretically should chill things down. Once again, if your top 10% of the people own stocks and everything else, average spending is not gonna go down.
turns.zh: 我想长端利率的上行最终会把我们抛进衰退，那理论上应该会让一切冷却下来。再说一遍，如果前 10% 的人拥有股票和一切，平均的支出不会下降。

turns.en: Median will, but average won't. And is that in order to get inflation to target? It's kind of waiting on Godot. I think we're 65 months north of target on core PCE.
turns.zh: 中位数会降，平均数不会降。——而这是为了让通胀回到目标？那简直是在等戈多。我想我们的核心 PCE 已经在目标之上 65 个月了。

turns.en: I think William said end of 2028, I think, 2% core PCE, it's a long way off and a lot of things can happen along the way. We've got fourish hikes priced into twos roughly, maybe three and a half from Fed funds to twos.
turns.zh: 我记得 Williams 说过，到 2028 年底核心 PCE 才回到 2%——路还很长，中间可能发生很多事。目前 2 年期国债大致定价了大约四次加息，从联邦基金利率到 2 年期大概是三次半。

turns.en: How do you see that evolving? It sounds to me like you might wanna fade that, that that's too aggressive, that there's just too many things that could prevent us from getting there.
turns.zh: 你怎么看这个演变？听你的意思，你可能想反着押这个——它太激进了，有太多东西可能阻止我们走到那一步。

turns.en: Tell us how you see monetary policy and the policy rate evolving. And is there anything to fade there? The best trade in the market right now is probably two year US Treasuries, up to 5%.
turns.zh: 告诉我们你怎么看货币政策和政策利率的演变。那里有什么可反押的吗？——现在市场上最好的交易大概是买 2 年期美国国债，收益率到 5%。

turns.en: You can't cry about that. You have almost no duration risk. You're locking in a rate that's state and local tax free. I've not been happy this last few months here.
turns.zh: 对这个你没理由抱怨。几乎没有久期风险，锁定的利率还免州税和地方税。——过去几个月我在这儿不太愉快。

turns.en: Last year, early this year when the market was pricing in three cuts, I was adamant higher for longer. Transitory is nonsense, rates ain't gonna move.
turns.zh: 去年、今年年初，当市场定价三次降息时，我坚决主张 higher for longer（更高更久）。暂时性是胡扯，利率不会往下走。

turns.en: I did not expect them to be hiking rates. I really not expect them to be hiking rates, pricing in three times. That was not on my bingo card.
turns.zh: 我没料到他们会加息。真的没料到加息会被定价三次。那不在我的 bingo 卡上。

turns.en: So I've been sad recently. To get twos higher than this, you're gonna have to go get a, I won't say a Volcker style Fed, but you gotta get a Fed that's gonna be jamming rates up to five.
turns.zh: 所以我最近有点郁闷。要让 2 年期比现在更高，你得有一个——我不会说是 Volcker 式的美联储——但得有一个愿意把利率猛怼到 5 的美联储。

turns.en: That's a hard call, man. I mean, cause I don't think it actually impacts the economy. As a matter of fact, I might even help the economy because all of a sudden, all these cash rich boomers and cash rich corporations, they're gonna earn more money on their accounts.
turns.zh: 那可真是个艰难的决定，伙计。因为我不认为它真的影响经济。事实上它甚至可能帮忙，因为所有那些现金充裕的婴儿潮退休者和现金充裕的公司，突然能在账户上赚到更多钱。

turns.en: I think I saw something from Albert Edwards that that interest income or expense from US corporations is actually positive now. They're earning more money than they're paying out an interest expense.
turns.zh: 我想我看到 Albert Edwards 说过，美国企业的利息收支现在实际上是正的——它们赚的利息比支付的利息费用还多。

turns.en: I could have this wrong, but I think it's pretty close to being zippers, which kind of means taking rates up actually increases the economy.
turns.zh: 我可能记错了，但我觉得相当接近这个状态，这意味着加息实际上在推高经济。

turns.en: It was kind of crazy. I think that's such an interesting one to debate, which is no one's making more money on this than Warren Buffett, right?
turns.zh: 挺疯狂的。我觉得这是个很有意思的辩论，而这件事上没人赚得比 Warren Buffett 更多，对吧？

turns.en: I think he's got 380 billion in short data treasuries. So you're just cutting a check to him. It's coming straight from the US government. And it is less than clear what taking the short rate up does.
turns.zh: 我想他有 3800 亿美元的短期国债。这等于政府直接给他开支票。而把短端利率抬上去到底会产生什么效果，实在没那么清楚。

turns.en: You know, there's winners and losers, but it's unclear if it's actually a headwind to future growth. And I think maybe that's where you just don't know exactly what policy is doing right now.
turns.zh: 你知道，有赢家就有输家，但它是否真的构成未来增长的逆风并不清楚。我觉得也许这正是问题：你根本说不准政策此刻在干什么。

turns.en: I think those concerns are real. I don't think moving rates up or down by 100 impacts the economy at all because you have the private banks making clones and the hyperscalers and everyone else.
turns.zh: 我认为这些担忧是真实的。我不认为利率上下 100 个基点会对经济有多大影响，因为有非银行机构在放贷，有 hyperscalers，还有各种各样的其他主体。

turns.en: I do think that taking rates down at this stage of the game would be a fine idea, except it's going to make Warsh look like he's a Trump sycophant, which he can't do.
turns.zh: 我确实认为，在现阶段降息是个不错的主意，只是那会让 Warsh 看起来像是 Trump 的马屁精，而他不能这样。

turns.en: That's why I think we're at 50 base points, one and done. He's proven he's not beholden to the president. And then he can go and maneuver from there.
turns.zh: 所以我认为这就是 50 个基点、一次搞定的原因。他已经证明自己不受总统牵制，然后他就可以从那个位置开始腾挪。

turns.en: He just didn't have the votes to go and do it. And having 12.0 as a public policy concept was a good thing. This is a political issue. And probably term limits would be the number one solution to this whole thing.
turns.zh: 他只是没有足够的票去做这件事。而把 2% 作为一个公共政策概念是好事。这是一个政治问题。而解决这一整套问题，任期限制也许才是头号方案。

turns.en: It would take away the motivation to keep, you know, kicking the can down the road because all of a sudden you see the various Republicans were no longer running.
turns.zh: 任期限制会消除那种继续把问题往后踢的动机，因为你突然会看到一些共和党人不再竞选连任了。

turns.en: All of a sudden they've seen Jesus and want to go and contain policy. Maybe we should have polio vaccines. MMT, which I always thought was total nonsense.
turns.zh: 突然他们就开始见着耶稣，想要约束政策了。也许我们也该给这事打一针小儿麻痹疫苗。现代货币理论（MMT）——我一直觉得那是纯粹的胡说八道。

turns.en: Notwithstanding the books written about it, long papers and everything else. MMT was you could borrow as much as you want until you get inflation from borrowing or lending or printing money.
turns.zh: 不管人们为它写了多少书、多少长篇论文。MMT 说的是：你可以随便借，直到借款、放贷或印钱带来通胀为止。

turns.en: And then once you get the inflation, you cut spending or raise taxes. That's true. I believe in that. The flaw is you can't do that. Politicians can't cut spending or raise taxes.
turns.zh: 而通胀一旦出现，你就削减支出或加税。这话是对的，我相信这一点。缺陷在于：你做不到。政客们既削减不了支出，也加不了税。

turns.en: It was a false God. Because you're relying upon this notion that people will do the right thing against their self-interest when the time is right.
turns.zh: 所以它是一尊假神。因为它依赖于这样一个假设：人们会在关键时刻违背自身利益去做正确的事。

turns.en: And they didn't. I mean, what I would do, I'm a libertarian basically, so don't get hung up on, I'm not a socialist. What they're probably going to do is they're going to uncap Social Security, 184,000 to unlimited.
turns.zh: 而他们并没有。我是说，如果换我会怎么做——我本质上是个自由至上主义者（libertarian），所以别误会，我不是社会主义者。他们大概率会做的是：取消社保缴费的工资上限，从 18.4 万美元取消到无限。

turns.en: They're going to make Social Security Medicare or other means test it, which is fine. They're going to go and get rid of the step-up basis. You want to go and push money to your kids, that's fine, but it's idea of step-up basis, you're stealing money from the government.
turns.zh: 他们会把社保、Medicare 或其他福利做经济状况调查（means test），这没问题。他们会取消阶梯式计税基础（step-up basis）。你想把钱传给子女可以，但 step-up basis 这个概念就是从政府手里偷钱。

turns.en: You bought an asset, went up in price, pay your taxes. I think things like that can significantly raise revenues, reduce that spread. A wealth tax is meaningless because you can just game that thing.
turns.zh: 你买了一项资产，它涨价了，你就该为此缴税。我认为这类措施能显著增加收入、缩小那个缺口。财富税则毫无意义，因为你总能把它规避掉。

turns.en: It's never worked in Europe, it's not going to work in the US. We have plenty of lawyers who go find ways to get around these things. Just making it so the rich upper classes pay a little more is fine.
turns.zh: 它在欧洲从来没成功过，在美国也不会成功。我们有的是律师去想办法绕过这些东西。让富裕的上层阶级多付一点点是可行的。

turns.en: We had a balanced budget, we had a surplus 25 years ago. There was a story from Page of the Journal saying bond traders look for new jobs because there'll be no treasuries in 15 years.
turns.zh: 25 年前我们有预算平衡，有盈余。《华尔街日报》有位记者写过一篇报道：债券交易员开始另找工作，因为 15 年后就不会有国债了。

turns.en: They'll all be paid off and that'll be that. Can you believe that? We had a surplus in 2001. There was no need for all these tax cuts. We could have been on a reasonable path.
turns.zh: 全都还清，故事结束。你能相信吗？2001 年我们有盈余。根本不需要后来那些大规模减税。我们本可以走上一条合理的道路。

turns.en: We had just gotten done doing social security adjustments. This is a self-inflicted wound that didn't have to happen. I am one of those upper-end people, I would pay more tax, I would pay more taxes, no, but I also think that sustaining the US enterprise is a good idea and I've done well because I've lived in the US where we have the rule of law and control the seas and have a rule of reserve currency.
turns.zh: 我们刚刚完成社保改革。这是一场完全可以避免、却自己捅出来的刀伤。我就是那种高收入人群，我愿意多缴税。我也认为维持美国这个事业是好事，我能混得好，正是因为我生活在美国——一个有法治、掌控海洋、拥有储备货币的国家。

turns.en: I'll paper a smaller favor. Let's do a little tutorial on your move index. You created it, I want to say 1988, is that correct? I actually created it in 94, but I had data going back to 88.
turns.zh: 那就请你帮个小忙。——我们来给你的 MOVE 指数做个小教学。你创造它，我想是 1988 年，对吗？——其实是 94 年做的，但数据可以回溯到 88 年。

turns.en: So the move index actually goes back for the mix. Okay, so it's been around a long time and as have you. So you mentioned 1994, that's another big bond market sell-off that was a famous event, Orange County, where you are now getting caught up in that, unfortunately, Robert Citron.
turns.zh: 所以 MOVE 指数实际回溯那么久。好，它存在很久了，你也一样。你提到 1994 年——那是另一场著名的大债市抛售事件，Orange County，不巧，跟你现在正被卷进去的那桩事有关，Robert Citron。

turns.en: I was at Merrill Lynch when it happened. Unbelievable, structured notes, Merrill Lynch and other firms proctoring gamble, Gibson greetings, right?
turns.zh: 事情发生时我在 Merrill Lynch。难以置信——结构化票据，Merrill Lynch 和其他一些公司在兜售这些豪赌，Gibson 式的问候，对吧？

turns.en: I mean, amazing event. So first of all, give us just a very quick tutorial on the move index and its calculation. And then I just want you to help contextualize what you see now just across the hundred.
turns.zh: 所以先给我们快速讲一遍 MOVE 指数及其计算方法，然后我想请你帮我们定位一下：现在它在 100 上方意味着什么。

turns.en: So first tell us the calc and then let's just talk about what information it's telling the market right now. The VIX and the move, they're called an index, but they're not like an index where they're based at a hundred on some date.
turns.zh: 先讲计算，然后我们谈谈它此刻在向市场传递什么信息。——VIX 和 MOVE 名字里带指数，但它们不是那种在某一天以 100 为基准的指数。

turns.en: And then you look at the price going up, then you measure the total move and then the monthly move or quarterly move. It's not that, it's actually a real number.
turns.zh: 不是你去盯价格上涨、然后度量总涨幅、月度或季度涨幅那种东西。它是一个实实在在的数字。

turns.en: It's an applied volatility. So the VIX right now is 16, easy rule. Divide the VIX by 16, actually 15.9. And that is the expected daily move of the S&P or anything you have out there.
turns.zh: 它是隐含波动率。VIX 现在是 16，简单的规则：把 VIX 除以 16——实际是 15.9——得到的就是标普或者任何你看的资产的预期日波动。

turns.en: Just look at the implied vol of any stock. Now by 16, that's the implied daily move. That's what the market is pricing in as the volatility of the asset.
turns.zh: 随便看一只股票的隐含波动率，除以 16，就是隐含的日波动。那就是市场定价中的该资产波动率。

turns.en: The move, similarly, is a real number. A move of a hundred means that the market, I would say expects, but it is implying that we will be within a hundred basis points up and down.
turns.zh: MOVE 同理，是一个实实在在的数字。MOVE 为 100，意思是市场——我不会说预期，而是隐含——利率将上下波动 100 个基点以内。

turns.en: So now we're at like five and a quarter on tens. We'll be between four and a quarter and six and a quarter, 60% of the time, a year from now.
turns.zh: 比如现在 10 年期大约在 5.25%。一年后的同一时点，10 年期会落在 4.25% 到 6.25% 之间，概率 60%。

turns.en: That's one standard deviation. That's what these numbers all mean. If you took stat ninth grade, you could be a professional option trader. There's nothing beyond stat 101 that we use.
turns.zh: 那是一个标准差。这些数字说的全是这个。你要是上过九年级的统计课，就能当专业期权交易员。我们用的东西超不出统计学 101。

turns.en: We put funny Greek words on it, delta gamma big. That's just nonsense to go, have us charge you a higher price. It's just ninth grade stat. One standard deviation is 68%.
turns.zh: 我们在上面套一些希腊字母，delta、gamma 什么的。那纯属胡扯，好让收费显得名正言顺。就是九年级统计：一个标准差对应 68%。

turns.en: And that's what it means. If we had a move of 60, that'd mean up and down 60 basis points a year from now, 60% of the time. Now, you take that hundred and I gave you a hundred basis points up and down annual number.
turns.zh: 意思就是这个。如果 MOVE 是 60，意思是从现在起一年后，利率上下波动 60 个基点以内的概率 60%。好，你拿 100，我给你的是 100 个基点的年度上下波动。

turns.en: Let's de-annualize the divide by 16 to get the daily for the VIX. That's implying the 68% chance that SAP will be up and down 16%. Hasn't changed.
turns.zh: 我们把它去年化——像 VIX 那样除以 16——得到日度数字。这意味着标普有 68% 的概率日波动 1% 上下（16 除以 16）。这个规律从没变过。

turns.en: 100 divided by 16 is like six and change. The market's pricing in for the next month, we're gonna move six basis points a day up or down. That's all it says.
turns.zh: 100 除以 16 大概是六多一点。市场定价的是：未来一个月，我们每天上下波动 6 个基点。它说的就是这个。

turns.en: And you've got a duration waiting though. There's a couple of underlines in there, expires. So clearly twos and tens and thirties of different animals.
turns.zh: 不过它有个久期加权。里面有几处下划线：到期日。显然 2 年期、10 年期、30 年期是不同的物种。

turns.en: What I did was I said, let's take the one month number, the volatility of twos, which is right now like 115. 20% of that, 20% of the five year, 40 of the 10 year, 20 of the bond, add them up and that's your move.
turns.zh: 我做的事情是：拿一个月期的数字——2 年期国债的波动率，现在大概 115——取它的 20%，5 年期的 20%，10 年期的 40%，长债的 20%，加总起来就是你的 MOVE。

turns.en: So there's times when you see like when the Fed was doing massive QE, the twos might be 40, but the thirties might be 80. When the Fed's active, right now you have twos at 115 and bonds at 85.
turns.zh: 所以有些时候，比如美联储在大规模 QE 时，2 年期可能是 40，但 30 年期是 80。美联储活跃的时候就是这样。而现在你看到的是 2 年期 115、长债 85。

turns.en: Twos are much more volatile than bonds. At least for now. That's it. That's what the move is, just a real number. By the way, I would say using these tools for either trading, not the bonds, but trading equities or gold or oil options, look at the implied vol divided by 16.
turns.zh: 2 年期比长债波动大得多。至少目前是这样。就这样，MOVE 就是这么回事，一个实实在在的数字。顺便说一句，我要说，用这些工具去做交易——不是做债券，而是做股票、黄金或原油期权——看隐含波动率除以 16。

turns.en: If you think that they're gonna move more or less than that number, then you could do a trade, a buy or a sell, or at least support a buy or a sell.
turns.zh: 如果你觉得实际的波动会比那个数字大或小，你就可以做一笔交易，买入或卖出，或者至少支持一个买入或卖出的决定。

turns.en: When Silver was doing crazy, Jan Beb, he had like a hundred and changed dollars. The vol was like 120. He was utterly insane. So I went and sold some strangles on that because I just did not think Silver was gonna go and be moving that much every day or a year moved that far.
turns.zh: 白银疯狂那阵子——它冲到 100 多美元的时候——隐含波动率有 120。那完全疯了。所以我去卖了一些宽跨式（strangles），因为我根本不信白银每天会动那么大、或者一年能走那么远。

turns.en: You had to scale it right. That's how I used it. What's the vol of an asset? I make a decision to make things be more or less than that. The interest rate market, you'd go back long enough and it certainly evolves in terms of its participants.
turns.zh: 你得把规模做对。我就是这么用它：资产的波动率是多少？我决定实际情况会比它大还是比它小。利率市场，如果你回溯足够久，它的参与者肯定是演化变化的。

turns.en: You don't have the old days of Fannie and Freddie doing lots of convexity hedging as they were. You don't have the government, Ben Bernanke and company buying bonds and pushing the move down to 40 and 50 in 2015 and 16.
turns.zh: 你已经没有 Fannie 和 Freddie 大量做凸性对冲（convexity hedging）的年代了。你也没有 Bernanke 那帮人买债券、在 2015、16 年把 MOVE 压到 40、50 的局面了。

turns.en: So the setup changes, the actors within the market change. When you look at a move of a hundred, that's certainly in an elevated percentile, 2022 tightening cycle higher.
turns.zh: 所以格局变了，市场里的角色变了。当你看到 MOVE 在 100，那肯定处在一个偏高的百分位——比 2022 年紧缩周期还高。

turns.en: That was aggressive. Of course, any crisis period, it's gonna be extremely high. When you look at a hundred on the move, just tell us what you see in terms of value, what sort of trade ideas does it inspire for you?
turns.zh: 那是很猛烈的。当然，任何危机时期它都会极高。当你看到 MOVE 在 100，就告诉我们你看到什么价值、它让你想到什么样的交易思路？

turns.en: Give us the Harley read. I'm not a believer in the fourth turning per se, but I do buy into the concept of every 80 years we kind of repeat history.
turns.zh: 给我们 Harley 式的解读。——我并不真的信第四次迁徙（Fourth Turning）那套，但我确实认同每隔 80 年历史会大体重复这个概念。

turns.en: Why is that? Well, you know your parents or their name, you know what they've done and did. Your grandparents, I know their names, didn't even kind of idea of their lives and what they did.
turns.zh: 为什么这么说？你认识你的父母，知道他们做过什么。你的祖父母——我知道他们的名字——你对他们的生活和经历几乎没有概念。

turns.en: Your great grandparents, I suspect you have no idea who they even are. And that's the issue here is that we have no first-hand recollection of things going back.
turns.zh: 你的曾祖父母，我猜你根本不知道他们是谁。而问题就在这里：我们对过去的事情没有任何第一手的记忆。

turns.en: So therefore, when something happens to you, you think it's new, but it's not, it's just the same thing happening. Over again, you haven't thought about it.
turns.zh: 所以当一件事发生在你身上，你以为它是新的，其实不是——同样的事情以前发生过，只是你没想过。

turns.en: We had rates down at one, two, three percent, the middle part of like over 10 years. And after a while, it's like, okay, great, you're supposed to trade at three and that's what they are and I bet that's kind of the world.
turns.zh: 利率在 1%、2%、3% 的低位置待了十多年。时间长了，你就觉得：好吧，就应该在 3，世界大概就应该是这样。

turns.en: You had 15 years of memory of anything before that. All of this is going back to the future. A 5% 10 year is basically where we've always been.
turns.zh: 对那之前的事你只有 15 年的记忆。而这一切都是在《回到未来》。5% 的 10 年期利率，基本上就是我们一直以来的常态位置。

turns.en: So it has not been a blowout, we just put the thumb off the scale. And we've gotten to where you're supposed to go. The thing is, of course, is that we always overshoot, so that's gonna happen.
turns.zh: 所以这不算离经叛道，我们只是把秤砣挪开了，回到了它本应在的地方。问题在于，我们当然总会超调，所以那也会发生。

turns.en: And the move, go pull up your move chart and look at the 90s, it averaged 100. My rule of thumb in the 90s was buy 80, sell 120. The problem with that is that when you get to 120, 130, the market is so bat-checked crazy that you're not in the mood to go sell options, you're hiding under your desk calling for your mommy.
turns.zh: 至于 MOVE，去把你的 MOVE 图拉出来看看 90 年代，它的均值是 100。我在 90 年代的经验法则是：80 买、120 卖。麻烦在于，当你到 120、130 的时候，市场已经疯得不像话，你根本没心情卖期权——你躲在桌子底下喊妈妈。

turns.en: And when the move gets to 60 or 70, the market's not moving at all. Why would you ever go and spend money? It's kind of like, why would you buy fire insurance on your house if it's raining outside?
turns.zh: 而当 MOVE 到 60、70，市场几乎不动。你为什么要花钱？就像——外面下着雨，你为什么要给房子买火灾险？你不会买的。

turns.en: You don't. So people can't buy 60, even though they should. And they can't sell 130, but they clearly should. But that was the old range, so being at 100 right now, it looks like it's up a lot, but it's not.
turns.zh: 所以人们在 60 不敢买，尽管他们应该买；在 130 不敢卖，尽管他们显然应该卖。但那就是旧的区间，所以现在在 100，看着好像涨了很多，其实没有。

turns.en: It's just gone back to where it used to be, which was 100. That was the old average for a decade. Well, what we've seen so far is the equity market, let's just use the S&P.
turns.zh: 它只是回到了它曾经的位置，也就是 100。那是一个十年的旧均值。——好，我们迄今看到的是股票市场，就用标普举例。

turns.en: I mean, it's got a ton of components and there's so much offset underneath the surface of the S&P, but it's flatlining. For the most part, it's just chopping, realize volatility is very low.
turns.zh: 我是说，它有很多成分，标普表面之下有太多的对冲抵消，但它基本是横着的。大部分时间就是震荡，已实现波动率非常低。

turns.en: There's a lot of breathless commentary on places like Twitter around tipping points. The bond market's about to take down the stock market. Where do you come out in terms of the vulnerability of the S&P to rates going higher from here?
turns.zh: 在 Twitter 之类的地方，有很多关于临界点的耸动评论：债市就要拖垮股市了。关于标普对利率从此处继续上行的脆弱性，你站哪一边？

turns.en: Do you think we're close or is this the market just saying, as you just kind of alluded to, look, rates can go up, the economy strong, nominal growth is strong, move on?
turns.zh: 你觉得我们快到了吗？还是就像你刚才暗示的，市场只是在说：看，利率可以涨，经济很强，名义增长很强，往前走？

turns.en: There is a point where rates impact stocks on a valuation basis. If only because a stock is a series of cash flows out the next 50 years, discounted back to a current present value.
turns.zh: 在估值层面，利率确实存在一个开始冲击股票的点。哪怕只是因为：一只股票本质上是未来 50 年的一系列现金流，折现回今天的现值。

turns.en: And so if you take long-term rates from three to five, you will go and reduce the value of those cash flows in today's terms. Take 0.97 to the 50th or 0.95, you get very different numbers.
turns.zh: 所以如果你把长期利率从 3% 抬到 5%，这些现金流的今天价值就会被压低。拿 0.97 的 50 次方和 0.95 的 50 次方，你会得到很不一样的数字。

turns.en: So yes, there is a value. The thing is value inequities is meaningless. I urge all of you to go find a YouTube of Michael Green, my good friend and partner, look at the half-hour version of it, not the longer one, you don't need that.
turns.zh: 所以是的，存在价值效应。问题是，眼下谈股票估值没有意义。我强烈建议你们都去 YouTube 上找 Michael Green——我的好朋友和搭档——的演讲，看 30 分钟那个版本，不用看长的，你不需要。

turns.en: And he's going to describe to you why passive is driving the market right now. And this is 100% right. What's happening right now is money is going into the market as millennials.
turns.zh: 他会给你讲清楚为什么现在是被动投资在驱动市场。这 100% 正确。现在正在发生的是：随着千禧一代进场，钱源源不断流入市场。

turns.en: What do I feel like it's to do? Maxsector 401K, it's tax-free money. Get the matching money from your employer, just free money. It's almost immediate investing, even better.
turns.zh: 那是什么在驱动？就是 401(k)：税优的钱，还有雇主匹配的免费的钱。这几乎是自动在投资，甚至更好。

turns.en: 80% SPY, 20% some five-year IT fund, turn it on to auto reinvest and call me in 30 years. It doesn't matter what the price is, money keeps going in.
turns.zh: 80% 的 SPY，20% 的某个五年期基金，开着自动再投资，30 年后再来找我。价格是多少无所谓，钱一直在往里进。

turns.en: As long as you have money going into the market, because we have a 4.1 on the planet rate, you're going to have money flowing into these retirement accounts, and it will buy S&P at whatever price it is.
turns.zh: 只要有钱在流入市场——因为失业率是 4.1%——就会一直有钱流入这些退休账户，而它会以任何价格买入标普。

turns.en: There's no value construct. What happens on top of this is what's called the passive construct, which basically says when a dollar goes in, you're going to put five bucks in Apple and 10 cents into Mosaic.
turns.zh: 没有估值框架这回事。在这之上起作用的是所谓的被动结构（passive construct）：基本上是说，每流入一美元，就有五美元进 Apple，一毛钱进 Mosaic。

turns.en: The thing is the stock's liquidity is not proportional to its market cap. Apple is not as liquid as its market cap is, so therefore when the money goes into Apple, it moves Apple by more percent than does Mosaic because of the less liquidity, the inelasticity of that price.
turns.zh: 问题在于，个股的流动性与其市值不成比例。Apple 的流动性并不像它的市值那么大，所以当钱流入 Apple 时，它推高 Apple 的幅度会比 Mosaic 更大——因为它更不流动，价格缺乏弹性。

turns.en: And that's why you see the industry propel higher and higher as passive money flows in, the less liquid component of the top bulge, that keeps blowing and blowing the bubble.
turns.zh: 这就是为什么你看到那些板块被被动资金越推越高：越不流动的成分，市值的凸起被吹得越大，泡沫就这么一直膨胀。

turns.en: Not bubble, just moving it along. Of course, when you ever get selling, it'll be the reverse because you'll be selling five bucks of Apple that is less liquid than 10 cents of Mosaic.
turns.zh: 说泡沫也未必，只是在推着走。当然，一旦出现卖出，就会反向重演：因为你要卖掉的是流动性更差的五美元 Apple，而只卖一毛钱的 Mosaic。

turns.en: What will cause selling is the question then. Well, the answer is unemployment over 5%. Once my kids lose their jobs, well, if they do, they will stop putting money into their 401k plans.
turns.zh: 那么，什么会引发卖出？答案是失业率超过 5%。一旦我的孩子们丢了工作——如果真丢的话——他们就会停止向 401(k) 计划存钱。

turns.en: That's how much I take. You're going to have to go and take unemployment up to some number. Is it four and a half, five, five? I don't know, but some number where the money stops flowing into these passive strategies.
turns.zh: 那就是撤走的那部分。失业率得升到某个数字——是 4.5、5、还是 5 以上？我不知道——反正是那个让钱停止流入这些被动策略的数字。

turns.en: And then the boomers, they have their mandatory withdrawals. That has to happen. You have the selling of passive. There's no value concept anymore to the equity market.
turns.zh: 然后婴儿潮一代有强制提款，那是必须发生的。于是你就有被动的卖出。股票市场已经不再有估值概念了。

turns.en: It's just money flows in and out. And so you got to ask the question, when will that money flow stop? And the answer is not yet. Let's finish with some of your trade ideas that you highlight in some of your writing.
turns.zh: 只有资金的进出。所以你要问的问题是：那资金流什么时候停？答案是：还没有。——我们来收尾，聊聊你在文章里强调的一些交易思路。

turns.en: An old saying out there that I really like is take what the vol service gives you. You know, there's a set of prices out there. Sometimes they facilitate what you want to do.
turns.zh: 我很喜欢一句老话：接住波动率曲面给你的东西。市场上有那样一组价格，有时候它们促成你想做的交易，

turns.en: Sometimes they're headwinds to what you want to do. But you've always been really clever about using curves, whether it's roll down FX translation, vol curves to facilitate certain bets that you want to make.
turns.zh: 有时候它们对你想做的事构成逆风。但你一直非常善于利用曲线——不管是滚存收益（roll down）、外汇的利率平移，还是波动率曲面——来促成某些你想做的押注。

turns.en: Are there any that you're particularly interested in right now that just set up well in terms of being facilitated by the set of prices on hand?
turns.zh: 有没有什么交易，是你现在特别感兴趣的，恰好的是手头这组价格正好在为它提供助力？

turns.en: A forward rate is not a prediction. It's the market's break-even. I'll make up numbers. The one-year rate at 4% and the two-year rate at 5%.
turns.zh: 远期利率不是预测，它是市场的盈亏平衡点。我随便编个数：一年期利率 4%，两年期利率 5%。

turns.en: And the question is, which one do I do? If I buy the one-year today for a year and then roll it over, I have to get 6% ignoring compounding.
turns.zh: 问题是，我选哪个？如果今天买一年期，持有一年，然后滚存，我——忽略复利——必须拿到 6% 的下一个一年期利率：第一年赚 4，第二年赚 6，平均 5，等于两年期利率。

turns.en: The next one-year rate, so I earn four, I earn six, I get five, which is the two-year rate. So you think the one-year rate's not gonna be at 6% next year, even by the two-year.
turns.zh: 所以你觉得明年的一年期利率不会是 6%，才轮得到两年期这个价。这只是那里的计算。6% 不是预测，只是那两个点之间的盈亏平衡。你可以把这个逻辑用在任何工具上——利率，或者波动率。

turns.en: That's just the calculation there. And the 6% is not a prediction, just the break-even between those two points. You can use that on any instrument, an interest rate or volatility.
turns.zh: 过去十年当曲线完全疯掉的时候，曾有过一些极好的机会。不幸的是，波动率曲面和利率曲线现在都非常平。

turns.en: And there were some incredible opportunities in the last decade when these curves have gotten totally crazy town. Unfortunately, the ball surface and the rate surface are dead flat right now.
turns.zh: 世上从来没有免费的午餐，但有些时候赔率是向你倾斜的。比如今年早些时候，当市场定价三次加息，你可以去看一年远期利率，然后说：天哪，这完全是错误的价格。因为按定价，我们得在一年后有一个 2.5% 的一年期利率——

turns.en: There's never been a free lunch, but there are times when the odds are tipped in your favor. So earlier this year, when you had three hikes priced in, you could go to the one-year rate, one-year forward and say, man, that's just the wrong price, but we're not gonna see that rate down there because of applying, you had to have a 2.5% one-year rate a year from now.
turns.zh: 那是不可能的事。所以你去做空那个利率。现在的曲线非常平，所以你什么也没有。而标普那边，波动率曲线略微向上倾斜。

turns.en: That was insanity. That's not gonna happen. So you go short that rate there. The curve's dead flat here, so you got nothing. And S&P is, that ball is a little upward sloping.
turns.zh: 加上利率高于标普的股息率，这会让标普的远期价格更高。唯一看起来有意思、而我却不想做的交易，是在标普上卖看涨、买看跌。

turns.en: And with rates being over S&P dividend yield, that also makes the S&P forward higher. The only trade that looks interesting, which I don't wanna do, would be to go sell calls and buy puts on the S&P.
turns.zh: 我不想做，因为我刚说过：只要失业率低、不发生变化，我觉得股票在这里没问题。如果我真觉得情况会不同，标普的远期价格是升水的——

turns.en: And I don't wanna do it because I just said, I think stocks are fine here, as long as unemployment is low, foreign change. If I did think it was gonna be otherwise, the forward price of the S&P is above.
turns.zh: 你可以看到这一点：看 SPX，再看期货合约，你会发现期货高出一定的数。那纯粹是标普的股息率和隔夜融资成本之间的算术差。

turns.en: And you could tell this, just look at SPX and look at the futures contract. And you see that the futures is higher by some number. That's strictly a calculation of the div rate of spools and the overnight financing rate of spools.
turns.zh: 而这里就给了你一个巨大的优势——前提是你想要做空。它会让价外看跌期权更便宜：你以为你买的是较当前点位 10% 价外的 put，

turns.en: And that gives you a huge advantage right here, but you gotta wanna be short. It wouldn't make out of the money puts cheap or cheaper because you might think you're buying a 10% out of the money put on the current level, but it might be a 12, 13, 14% out of the money put in the model, so that would make it cheaper.
turns.zh: 但在模型里它可能是 12%、13%、14% 价外的 put，所以它实际上更便宜。如果你想对冲，标普的价外看跌期权大概是你最好的对冲。

turns.en: That's probably your best, if you wanted a hedge, S&P out of the money puts are probably your best hedge. But once again, I'm not advising that because I just don't see a hard break in the market.
turns.zh: 但我还是不建议，因为我确实看不到市场会出现那种断裂式下跌。

turns.en: I guess if we got rates up to six, which we can be there in a week for God's sakes, I guess that might at some point, rates will impact S&P, it will.
turns.zh: 我想，如果利率升到 6%——天知道，我们可能一周之内就在那儿——我想到了某个时刻，利率会影响标普，会的。

turns.en: If only because people should sell S&P and buy bonds to lock in the return. That's a market timing issue, which is like, well, but my pig rate.
turns.zh: 哪怕只是因为人们应该会卖标普、买债券来锁定回报。这就是个择时问题，类似于那种：可我已经有收益在里面了。

turns.en: I'll give you just one last request to just riff on this, which is there's the old saying, the cure for higher prices is higher prices, just around demand destruction, maybe that's in crude.
turns.zh: 最后请你即兴聊一个观点：老话说高价的解药是更高的价格，讲的是需求毁灭，也许那在原油上是成立的。

turns.en: And it seems to me that the cure for higher rates is higher rates. You just kind of went there, which is at some point, you tell me if you agree with this or not, but these rates get high enough, they just sow the seeds for an equity risk off that kind of brings rates lower.
turns.zh: 而在我看来，高利率的解药是更高的利率。你刚才其实也说到那儿去了：到了某一点，你看这些利率高到一定程度，它们自己就会为一场股市避险（risk off）播下种子，从而把利率带下来。

turns.en: If you destroy the economy, you're gonna just take out any inflation premium, growth premium that might be embedded in five and a quarter, 10 years, if the risk off is serious enough.
turns.zh: 如果经济被摧毁，那么 5.25% 的 10 年期里可能内嵌的任何通胀溢价、增长溢价都会被抹掉——如果那场 risk off 足够严重。你同意吗？你怎么看这件事？

turns.en: Do you agree with that? How do you think through that? I agree with your principle of the cure for high prices is high prices. This we completely with the notion that it's gonna work in interest rates.
turns.zh: 你觉得那会实现吗？你怎么想？——我同意高价的解药是高价这个原则，但对于它在利率上也成立，我不完全认同。

turns.en: I think if we're working in oil, they're choking this thing off and probably seeing demand destruction of some kind. Well, I was not going crazy yet.
turns.zh: 我想在石油上它可能正在起作用，正在掐住需求、造成某种需求毁灭。——嗯，之前市场还没那么疯狂。

turns.en: Well, it's gone a little crazy. But I'm for bonds. I already said the hyperscalers will issue at any price. 20% would they do it? No, if Oracle goes from six to eight, you know, meta goes from seven to nine, does that matter?
turns.zh: 好吧，是有点疯狂了。但我看好债券。我已经说过 hyperscalers 会在任何价格发行。20% 它们也发？不会。但如果 Oracle 从 6 涨到 8、Meta 从 7 涨到 9，有什么关系？

turns.en: Not one lick. They're fighting this existential for these guys. Existential risk for these guys. They're not the ones who win. The US government, there is no price where they'll stop borrow.
turns.zh: 一点关系都没有。对它们来说这是生死之战，是存在性风险。它们不是能赢的那几家。而美国政府，不存在让它们停止借款的价格。

turns.en: They have to borrow. We'll say default. So therefore, we have the two biggest borrowers, basically $2.7 trillion, who are totally price insensitive.
turns.zh: 它们必须借。否则就是违约。所以我们面对的是最大的两个借款者——合计大约 2.7 万亿——完全对价格不敏感。

turns.en: So I don't see how that matters. Yes, will credit card guys buy fewer things? Yeah, sure. Will car loans stop car sales? Yes, will the mortgage market get hurt?
turns.zh: 所以我看不出高利率怎么会管用。是，信用卡的人会少买东西吗？会。车贷会抑制卖车吗？会。按揭市场会受伤吗？会。

turns.en: Yes, but the two biggest guys out there are price insensitive. Let me rephrase it a little bit. Suppose unemployment does go to 5%. Suppose the VIX goes to 30 and the stock market sells off considerably.
turns.zh: 但市场上最大的两个玩家对价格不敏感。——我换个说法：假设失业率真的升到 5%，假设 VIX 到 30，股市大跌。

turns.en: You know, it's a 10 to 15% drawdown. Do you think rates are lower from here? Or do they keep going up even in the face of a nasty shock to the equity market?
turns.zh: 你知道，一个 10 到 15% 的回撤。你觉得利率会比现在低吗？还是说即便面对股市的猛烈冲击，它们仍然继续往上？

turns.en: Front end goes down hard. Everyone moves to bills, two years on end. We'll go down by 100. So it's probably a bull steeping event. Yes, it was bull steeping.
turns.zh: 短端会大幅下来。所有人都涌向国库券。2 年期会下来 100。所以那大概是一次牛市变陡（bull steepening），就是 bull steepening。

turns.en: Okay. 30s go, I don't know. 10s go, it was less. But I mean, it'll be a massive steepener. If you have a VIX at 30, you'll choose down by 50, I don't know, something like that.
turns.zh: 30 年期怎样我不知道。10 年期会少一点。但我是说，那会是一次巨大的变陡。如果 VIX 到 30，报价大概会砍掉 50，我不知道，大概那样。

turns.en: Because if it's not hiking for sure, and once you pull the hike out, then long-term funds to 2s is 50 bips. Right, so right now we have a 390 on funds.
turns.zh: 因为到那时肯定不会再加息。一旦你把加息从定价里拿掉，联邦基金到 2 年期的利差是 50 个基点。现在联邦基金在 3.90%。

turns.en: So you can put 2s at a 440. The trading 490 now. Okay, there you go. Once again, we overshoot and undershoot. I'm just talking big picture, man.
turns.zh: 所以你可以把 2 年期看到 4.40%，它现在交易在 4.90%。就是这样。再说一遍，我们总会超调，也会欠调。我只是在大图上说，伙计。

turns.en: We know where fair value is. We're never at fair value, but we know where it is. It's just a better time. Well, Harley, it's great to catch up.
turns.zh: 我们知道公允价值在哪。我们从不在公允价值上，但我们知道它在哪，只是时机的差别。——好，Harley，跟你重新聊太好了。

turns.en: I appreciate you taking the invite on short notice. I definitely wanted to get your thoughts out there in front of the Alpha Exchange audience.
turns.zh: 感谢你临时应邀。我一定要把你的想法呈现给 Alpha Exchange 的听众。

turns.en: I know they'll be appreciated at a time when uncertainty is with us and probably not going away anytime soon. Thanks for being a guest. Excellent, thank you for hosting me.
turns.zh: 我知道在不确定如影随形、短期也不会离去的当下，大家会感激这些内容。谢谢你来做客。——太棒了，谢谢你邀请我。

turns.en: You've been listening to the Alpha Exchange. If you've enjoyed the show, please do tell a friend. And before we leave, I wanted to invite you to drop us some feedback.
turns.zh: 你刚才听的是 Alpha Exchange。如果你喜欢这档节目，请转告一位朋友。在我们结束之前，也邀请你给我们留一些反馈。

turns.en: As we aim to utilize these conversations to contribute to the investment community's understanding of risk, your input is valuable and provides direction on where we should focus.
turns.zh: 我们希望能借助这些对话，帮助投资界加深理解风险，你的意见很宝贵，为我们该聚焦哪里指明方向。

turns.en: Please email us at feedback at alphaexchangepodcast.com. Thanks again and catch you next time.
turns.zh: 请发邮箱 feedback@alphaexchangepodcast.com。再次感谢，下次见。
